summary.headline: Excel Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR281 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 11.8% to INR1,094 crore with adjusted EBITDA of INR112 crore (10.1% margin).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR281 crore (up 13% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA of INR22 crore (8% margin) and PAT of INR13 crore. Management attributed the weak first half to an extended monsoon and channel inventory build-up in agrochemical intermediates, and said demand turned in Q4. FY26 PAT was INR73 crore (6.7% margin) and the company reports zero long-term debt and net cash. A final dividend of INR13.75 per share (275% of INR5 face value) was declared. Management declined to give forward guidance, citing raw material volatility and monsoon uncertainty.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR11 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR13.75 per share (275% of INR5 face value)

segments.name: Chemicals - Agrochemical intermediates
segments.commentary: Largest product group (management indicated agrochemical intermediates are roughly 60% of revenue per an analyst's figure; not confirmed). Demand was weak in H1 FY26 and cyclical in Q3, with recovery seen in Q4.

segments.name: YP derivatives
segments.commentary: Management said good performance in YP derivatives partly offset the agrochemical intermediates cyclicality in Q3 FY26. Named as a growth driver with capex planned.

segments.name: Performance Solutions
segments.commentary: Performance Solutions also offset weakness in Q3 FY26. Includes biocides (2,530 tpa capacity addition operational in H2 FY26) and phosphonates, where domestic market share is 50-55%. Exports are largely from this group.

segments.name: Pharma intermediates and APIs / contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Contract manufacturing LTA with a multinational (announced May 2024) is progressing with validation batches dispatched. A second agreement (Nov 2025) is on track, with dedicated capacity expected by July 2026.

segments.name: Waste management
segments.commentary: Approximately 1% of revenues; management said it continues to operate steadily.

guidance_outlook: No forward financial guidance; management said it is not possible to make forward statements given raw material and monsoon uncertainty.
Contract manufacturing dedicated line expected to be commissioned by July 2026.
One more biocide product to be launched in H2 FY27 (second half of FY26-27 financial year as stated).

Indicative capex of INR200-300 crore over next two to three years in Performance Solutions, contract manufacturing and YP derivatives; management indicated fixed asset turnover of 1-1.5x and expected ROI of 15-20%.
Management expects agrochemical intermediates' share of revenue to fall as higher-margin, value-accretive business is added.
capex_capacity: Biocides capacity addition of 2,530 tpa of existing product (announced March 2025) operational in H2 FY26.
Contract manufacturing dedicated line for the Nov 2025 agreement expected to be completed by July 2026.
Capacity utilisation at 65-85% depending on product (management); an analyst cited 70-75%, not disputed.
Total installed capacity not disclosed, citing commercial reasons.
New corporate R&D centre at Rabale, Navi Mumbai operationalised during FY26.
Indicative capex of INR200-300 crore over 2-3 years; no segment-wise breakdown given. Existing capex deployments referenced but not quantified.
demand_pricing: Agrochemical intermediates demand was hit in H1 FY26 by an extended monsoon and channel inventory build-up; the demand environment began turning in Q4 FY26.
Raw material prices and availability were disrupted by geopolitical developments in Q1 FY27; management said price increases were largely passed on in April and May 2026.

Pricing is moved to monthly or quarterly cycles, and shorter windows are being used for some products. Procurement of raw materials is largely spot-based, with yellow phosphorus sourced from Kazakhstan and Vietnam.
Chinese competition is intense; management said Chinese prices rose on withdrawal of China's VAT refund (April 2026), but gave no specific figures.

Phosphonates domestic market share is 50-55%. Exports (about 20% of revenue) are mainly from Performance Solutions to the US, EU, Latin America and Middle East. THP has a significant global market share, per management.
Management flagged risk to agrochemical intermediates demand from a possible sub-optimal monsoon due to El Nino forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: Aspiration for growth (10% or 15% CAGR) and why not a share buyback given the cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cyclicality and recommended a 10-year view rather than two years of EBITDA. It gave no growth target. The buyback suggestion was noted for Board discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of DGTR anti-dumping findings on HCDP and ATMP, and revenue exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Findings are expected by about September 2026 in normal course, but timing is outside the company's control. Management did not quantify revenue exposure and said it would revert.

qa_highlights.question: Capex ROI, asset turnover and timelines for the INR200-300 crore plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed asset turnover is 1-1.5x and expected ROI 15-20%. It would not disclose deployment details, promising disclosure of major capex when it happens.

qa_highlights.question: Installed capacity and capacity additions over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 65-85% by product. Total installed capacity was not shared for commercial reasons. Additions are planned in Performance Solutions, contract manufacturing and YP derivatives.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing strategy and any FY27 price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is dynamic and market-based. Input cost increases were largely passed on, and management aims to protect or grow market share against Chinese competition.

qa_highlights.question: Five-year vision to FY30 on revenue, export share, CDMO share and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: No numbers were given. Management said exports and contract manufacturing will rise as a share of the portfolio, and that it will consolidate in phosphorus chemistry rather than enter crowded areas.

risks_watch: Monsoon and El Nino risk to agrochemical intermediates demand in FY27.
Raw material (yellow phosphorus, sulfur) price and availability volatility; the company did not disclose the sulfur or yellow phosphorus share of costs.
Chinese competition and the withdrawal of China's VAT refund affecting prices.
Timing and outcome of the DGTR anti-dumping case on HCDP and ATMP (findings expected by about September 2026).
Commissioning of the contract manufacturing line by July 2026 and the biocide launch in H2 FY27.
Capital allocation: the cash pile and the low share price were questioned, and no buyback decision was announced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the recovery and long-term strategy, but evasive on quantitative detail: management declined to give growth targets, segment capex, installed capacity, R&D spend, revenue breakdown and the DGTR exposure. It repeatedly said that near-term uncertainty prevents forward statements.
key_quotes: So, specific to cyclicality, maybe there will be an improvement, but I can't comment specifically, you know, what will happen in the future.
It's typically the inbound that comes in from a customer, you know, seeking a specific query.
Given the overall uncertainty and volatility, it is not possible to make any forward statements.
